Author: G.Radha Rani
Bench: G.Radha Rani
 The Honourable Dr.Justice G.Radha Rani

Judgment:

This appeal is filed by the injured - claimant aggrieved by the award and decree dated 29.02.2012 passed in O.P.No.1277 of 2009 by the XXII Additional Chief Judge-cum-Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (for short "MACT"), City Criminal Court, Hyderabad.

entities.text: XXII Additional Chief Judge-cum-Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties are hereinafter referred as arrayed before the Tribunal.
3. The case of the claimant in brief was that he was aged about 42 years, working as a helper and was earning Rs.4,500/- per month by the date of accident on 28.10.2008.

On 28.10.2008 at 11:00 AM while he was going along with one Bhagavanthu on motor cycle bearing No.AP22AC7519 as a pillion rider from Jinnaram to Vundekodur and when reached near the turning of Vundekodur Village, a tractor and trailer bearing No.AP22U7205 and AP22U7206 driven by its driver with high-speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle on which the petitioner was travelling, in opposite direction, due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained fracture to his right thigh,
fracture of patella, crush injury to right foot, head injury and blunt injuries all over the body.
The rider of the motorcycle, Bhagavanthu also Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 sustained fracture injuries.

Immediately, both the rider and pillion-rider of the motorcycle were shifted to SVS Hospital,
Mahaboobnagar.
There, the petitioner was operated and steel rods were inserted.
The Police of PS Narva registered a case in Crime No.51 of 2008 against the driver of the tractor and trailer.

The petitioner contended that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trailer and as such claimed compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the tractor and trailer bearing No.AP22U7205 and AP22U7206.
4.

The respondent No.1 remained ex-parte.
5.
The respondent No.2 filed counter denying the petition averments.

The respondent No.2 called for strict proof of the age, occupation and income of the petitioner, that the accident occurred was due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and trailer and that the driver of the tractor and trailer was having a valid, effective and subsisting driving license to drive the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company also contended that the compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- claimed by the petitioner was excessive and exorbitant.

sentences.text: During the course of enquiry, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got examined the doctor, who issued the disability certificate, as PW.2.
The petitioner got marked Exs.A1 to A10 on his behalf.

Ex.A1 is the certified copy Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 of the FIR, Ex.A2 is the certified copy of the charge-sheet, Ex.A3 is the certified copy of the injury certificate, Ex.A4 is the discharge summary, Ex.A5 is the out-patient card, Ex.A6 are prescriptions, Ex.A7 is the disability certificate issued by PW.2, Ex.A8 is the estimation certificate, Ex.A9 is the salary certificate and Ex.A10 are the X-ray films.

The case-sheet of the petitioner at SVS Medical College Hospital, Mahaboobnagar was marked as Ex.X1.
7.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.

8. On considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal held that the petitioner sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing No.AP22U7205 and AP22U7206.
The said observation of the Tribunal was not challenged by the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, as such, the same holds good.

9. With regard to the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal on considering the evidence of PW.2,
the consultant Orthopedic Surgeon in Gandhi Hospital and who issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.A7, considered the disability sustained by the petitioner as 40% partial and permanent.

10. The Tribunal considered the age of the petitioner as 45 years as per the discharge summary of SVS Hospital, Mahaboobnagar and considered the Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 income of the petitioner as Rs.3,000 per month and applied multiplier "13" and calculated the loss of earnings due to the partial and permanent disability sustained by the petitioner as Rs.1,87,200/-.

The Tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses for removal of rods and awarded Rs.5,000/-
towards extra nourishment and Rs.5,000/- towards transportation and in total awarded an amount an amount of Rs.2,27,200/- with interest @ 9 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and held both the respondents 1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner - claimant.

11. Aggrieved by the said award and decree, the claimant filed this appeal contending that the compensation awarded was meager and the Tribunal went wrong in awarding less amount of compensation of Rs.2,27,200/- when the appellant was entitled to more than the claim amount of Rs.4,00,000/-.
The Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the appellant - claimant as Rs.4,500/- per month, but considered the same as only Rs.3,000/- per month.

The Tribunal ought to have considered the functional disability of the petitioner as 100% instead of 40% as assessed by the doctor and ought to have awarded an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities, social status, shock, mental agony, but awarded a meager amount of Rs.15,000/- under these heads.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering, but not awarded any amount separately under the said head.
The Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 Tribunal failed to award any amount towards loss of earnings though the appellant claimed an amount of Rs.40,000/- which was just and reasonable.

The Tribunal failed to award any amount towards nursing (attendant charges) though the appellant was bed-ridden completely for six (06) months K. Srinivasulu vs B.Manjula And Another on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6929754/
2 and ought to have awarded an amount of Rs.1,000/- towards damage to clothing and prayed to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation from Rs.2,27,200/- to Rs.4,00,000/-.
12.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.

13. As seen from the record, the age of the appellant-claimant was shown as 45 years in the charge-sheet and police records marked under Exs.A2 and A3 and also in the discharge summary marked under Ex.A4 but was shown differently in the out-patient cards as 40, 42 and 45 years and in Exs.A6 and A7 as 43 years.
Hence, the Tribunal rightly considered the age of the claimant as 45 years.
However, the Tribunal applied multiplier "13" that would apply for the age of 50 years.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation 1 , the appropriate multiplier for the ages between 41 to 45 years is "14".

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant - claimant filed a document headed as salary certificate issued by one K.Venkata Rami Reddy, marked under Ex.A9, which would disclose that the claimant worked as a helper on a paddy cutting machine and that he was paying Rs.4,500/- per month as salary to the claimant.
But the person who issued the salary certificate was not examined by the claimant as a witness before the Tribunal.
Hence, the Tribunal had not relied upon the said document to consider the income of the claimant as Rs.4,500/- per month.

15. But, even in the absence of any documentary proof, considering him as a labourer also, the income of the claimant can be considered as Rs.4,500/- per month by the date of accident on 28.10.2008 basing on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited2, wherein the income of a labourer was considered as Rs.4,500/- by the Hon'ble Apex Court for the accident occurred in the year 2004 itself.
16.

sentences.text: The evidence of PW.2 would disclose that he was a consultant Orthopedic Surgeon in Gandhi Hospital and was also practicing at Sai Speciality Clinic, Secunderabad, the claimant approached him at his clinic on 16.06.2009 with pain and stiffness of right hip and knee joint and pain and stiffness in the right shoulder.

He stated that he examined the prior records of 2011 LawSuit (SC)
830 Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 the claimant where he was treated at SVS Medical College Hospital, Mahaboobnagar and after examining the patient clinically and radiologically by getting relevant fresh X-rays, issued disability certificate marked under Ex.A7.

Ex.A7 would disclose that the patient sustained fracture of right femur, right patella and fracture of right clavicle and he was suffering with stiffness of right hip and right shoulder and the patient was unable to sit, squat, stand and walk normally and was unable to lift weights, as such, assessed the disability sustained by the petitioner - claimant as 40% partial and permanent.

17. The learned counsel for the appellant - claimant relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar and Another 3, wherein it was held that:

sentences.text: Disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human-being.

Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.
Temporary disability refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.

Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage IV (2010) ACC 815 (SC) Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.

The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (`Disabilities Act' for short).

entities.text: Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: But if any of the disabilities enumerated in section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.
7. The percentage of permanent disability is expressed by the Doctors with reference to the whole body, or more often than not, with reference to a particular limb.

When a disability certificate states that the injured has suffered permanent disability to an extent of 45% of the left lower limb, it is not the same as 45% permanent disability with reference to the whole body.

The extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) expressed in terms of a percentage of the total functions of that limb, obviously cannot be assumed to be the extent of disability of the whole body.

If there is 60%
permanent disability of the right hand and 80% permanent disability of left leg, it does not mean that the extent of permanent disability with reference to the whole body is 140% (that is 80% plus 60%).

If different parts of the body have suffered different percentages of disabilities, the sum total thereof expressed in terms of the permanent disability with reference to the whole body, cannot obviously exceed 100%.

8. Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
The Tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

In most of the cases, the percentage of economic loss, that is, Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 percentage of loss of earning capacity, arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability.

Some Tribunals wrongly assume that in all cases,
a particular extent (percentage) of permanent disability would result in a K. Srinivasulu vs B.Manjula And Another on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6929754/
4 corresponding loss of earning capacity, and consequently, if the evidence produced show 45% as the permanent disability, will hold that there is 45% loss of future earning capacity.

entities.text: K. Srinivasulu vs B.Manjula And Another on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In most of the cases, equating the extent (percentage) of loss of earning capacity to the extent (percentage) of permanent disability will result in award of either too low or too high a compensation.

What requires to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanently disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terns of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the standard multiplier method used to determine loss of dependency).

We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation

(see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra v. New India Assurance Co.Ltd. IV (2010) ACC 348 (SC) = VII (2010) SLT 239 = 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M.,
National Insurance Co. Ltd. III (2010) ACC 869 = VI (2010) SLT 426 = 2010 (8)
SCALE 567)."
18.

sentences.text: In the present case, the occupation of the appellant-petitioner was shown as a helper on a paddy cutting machine.
It was a seasonal work and might not be available for the whole year.
Hence, it can be safely presumed that the petitioner was an agricultural labourer.

As the physical disability sustained by the petitioner was stated by PW.2 as partial and permanent, this Court considers Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 the percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of such disability is approximately the same as the percentage of partial and permanent disability sustained by the petitioner and the Tribunal committed no error in considering the same as 40%.

Hence, the loss of earning capacity can be assessed as Rs.4,500 x 12 x 14 x 40/100 = Rs.3,02,400/-.
19.

As the appellant - claimant might not have attended to his work for a period of six (06) months due to these fracture injuries sustained by him, the loss of income during the period of his treatment can be considered as Rs.4,500 x 6 = Rs.27,000/-.
20.

As the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 would disclose that the petitioner - claimant sustained three (03)
fracture injuries (fracture of right femur, fracture of right patella and fracture of right clavicle) and the petitioner was suffering with stiffness of right hip, knee and shoulder, even two (02) years after the accident, it is considered fit to award an amount of Rs.60,000/- (Rs.20,000/- for each fracture injury) under this head.

21. As the estimation certificate marked under Ex.A8, issued by PW.2 would disclose that the appellant-claimant required another surgery for removal of rods / implants and the same was assessed as Rs.25,000/-, it is considered fit to award the said amount towards his future medical expenses.
The amounts of Rs.5,000/- towards extra nourishment and Rs.5,000/-towards transportation Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 awarded by the Tribunal are considered as appropriate and require no interference.

S.No .

Heads Compensation Awarded 1. Loss of earning capacity due Rs.3,02,400/-
to partial and permanent disability 2. Pain and Suffering Rs.60,000/-
3. Loss of earnings during the Rs.27,000/-
period of treatment (for a period of six months)

4. Future Medical Expenses Rs.25,000/-
5. Extra Nourishment Rs.5,000/-
6. Transportation Rs.5,000/-
The appellant - claimant claimed an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- only.

However, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sri Laxman @ Laxman Mourya v. Divisional Manager,
Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Another4 and in Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh5, it was held that in the absence of any bar in the Act, the Tribunal and any competent Court is entitled to award higher compensation to the victims of an accident.

Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Another4

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation where the interest of the claimants is of paramount consideration.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in several cases held that 2011 (10) SCC 756 2003 ACJ 12 (SC) Dr.GRR, J macma_2113_2012 the Court should make an endeavour to extend the benefit to the claimants, to award just and reasonable compensation to the extent possible.

Hence, it is considered fit to enhance the compensation from Rs.2,26,200/- awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.4,24,400/- which is considered as just and reasonable with interest @ 7.5 % per annum on the enhanced amount subject to payment of deficit court fee.

24. In the result, M.A.C.M.A.No.2113 of 2012 filed by the injured - claimant is allowed enhancing the compensation from Rs.2,27,200/- awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.4,24,400/- with interest @ 7.5 %
per annum on the enhanced amount.

The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the above amount within a period of six (06) weeks after deducting the amount deposited if any and the claimant is permitted to withdraw the above amount without furnishing any security, on payment of deficit court fee.
No order as to costs.
